questions.question:
Identify the correct sentence that uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A) Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B) So fast did he run that he broke the record.
C) Only after finishing all the tasks did she realize the time.
D) Hardly had she arrived when the meeting started.
options: Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
So fast did he run that he broke the record.
Only after finishing all the tasks did she realize the time.
Hardly had she arrived when the meeting started.
questions.answer: Only after finishing all the tasks did she realize the time.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail about the event?

A) It was John who called the meeting yesterday.
B) That John called the meeting yesterday was unexpected.
C) John was the one who called the meeting yesterday.
D) The meeting was yesterday that John called it.
options: It was John who called the meeting yesterday.
That John called the meeting yesterday was unexpected.
John was the one who called the meeting yesterday.
The meeting was yesterday that John called it.
questions.answer: It was John who called the meeting yesterday.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly completes the sentence with a third conditional structure.

If they ______ the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.

A) had known
B) knew
C) would have known
D) had been knowing
options: If they had known the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.
If they knew the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.
If they would have known the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.
If they had been knowing the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.
questions.answer: If they had known the weather forecast, they wouldn't have gone hiking in the storm.

questions.question:
Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood correctly to express a hypothetical wish or demand?

A) I suggest that he attends the conference.
B) It is essential that the documents be submitted by Friday.
C) If I were you, I would take that job.
D) We require that all employees submit their reports now.
options: I suggest that he attends the conference.
It is essential that the documents be submitted by Friday.
If I were you, I would take that job.
We require that all employees submit their reports now.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would take that job.

questions.question:
Identify the correct sentence that demonstrates ellipsis, where a word is omitted but understood from context.

A) She likes coffee, but he doesn't.
B) They are going to the cinema, and so am I.
C) He plays football, and she does too.
D) We finished the project, and they have.
options: She likes coffee, but he doesn't.
They are going to the cinema, and so am I.
He plays football, and she does too.
We finished the project, and they have.
questions.answer: They are going to the cinema, and so am I.
